Coming next: hosted Cube, hosted SLayer, hosted & queryable Snowflake Semantic View, hosted and & queryable Databricks Metric Views and Looker / LookML.

## Dex Semantics

Let your agent build analytics with 25% fewer errors, thanks to data that explains itself to your coding agent.

A join can keep running after the source changes underneath it, and quietly count every row twice. Dex Semantics keeps each model's meaning with the model, as code, so that kind of error is caught instead of shipped: [...] Dex Semantics: the declaration lives with your models (one row per shipment; production counts harvests; revenue uses the agreed price), Dex checks the built data (S01 and S02: expected 1 row, found 2; without Dex 200 t, with Dex 100 t), and the meaning flows to tests, semantic models and the next agent session 

25% fewer failed tasks on ADE-bench with Claude Sonnet 5.5 (15 against 20 of 75). The image is an illustrated workflow on synthetic data.

Dex Semantics · declarations · the film

## See it on a real project [...] More in the package README.

We run Dex on two public analytics-engineering benchmarks and commit every run's raw per-task results, including the ones that flatter us least.

| Benchmark | Setup | Result | Details |
 ---  --- |
| data-eng-bench (Snowflake, 103 tasks) | Dex + Claude Sonnet 5 | 57.3% resolved, 89.7% of assertions pass | README |
| ADE-bench (dbt Labs, 75 tasks) | Dex 1.17.4 + Claude Sonnet 5.5 | 80% resolved vs 73.3% without Dex; 25% fewer failures | README |

On ADE-bench, the same Claude Sonnet 5.5 model solves 60 of 75 tasks with Dex, compared with 55 without it: +6.7 percentage points, with net gains across six of seven projects. Both configurations make one scored attempt per task. Compare the runs and raw results.

results.content: Decision-makers I talk to want the flexibility to define their own analytics, at the speed of agents. They want to ask a question, agree on the metric definition, and have the answer before the question stops mattering. Engineers we talk to want that too. They also want changes they can review and fewer broken data contracts waking them up at 3AM. I believe both can and should be happy. And sleep at least eight hours per night. We give agents a workflow that connects a business question to tested, reviewable changes, and keeps them healthy checking the actual state of your warehouse. Enter Dex Enterprise: self-building analytics, owned by your team. Built on open-source Dex, it brings three workflows to the whole data team Scope: Turn an analytics goal into a concrete plan. results.content: change the game. Dex runs SLayer's own validation rules against your warehouse and returns every model, measure and join a change broke.  It checks every single declared primary key and join cardinality against the data, as it changes.  It then proposes the repair as a diff, cutting out exactly what the dropped column took with it. No more maintenance pain, and no more rigid BI-native semantics for your agents. SLayer by Motley:  Dex by Exmergo:  Thank you Yann Ranchere and the Motley team. Let's keep building the future of data, in the present. More details in the comments ↓ [...] Dex now works natively with SLayer, the agent-native semantic layer from Motley. Dex can now:   - read SLayer models straight from your repo   - write new ones from your dbt models   - run SLayer queries under its cost guard   - and as always, maintain the layer as your data changes Let's break it down. 1. How do you get from dbt to the semantic layer? With Dex, you can embed declarations throughout your dbt project. Declarations help your agent build better models downstream, and that includes the semantic layer. Creating a semantic layer is no longer a chore, it’s a natural progression of your data & analytics work. But not all semantic layers are created equal, especially for agents. 2. Which semantic layer is the best for your agent? This is where SLayer by Motley fits. Semantic [...] your agent? This is where SLayer by Motley fits. Semantic layers were designed for rigid BI dashboards. But agents need more flexibility: a ratio, last year against this year, an average where the dashboard had a sum. In SLayer you define revenue once, and the agent can ask for sum(revenue), avg(revenue), or the same sum shifted back by a year. It’s built around how your agent actually retrieves data: search, inspect, query. It speaks MCP, REST, a CLI and Python, and the models are YAML files in your repo. 3. And what about maintenance? A semantic layer is one more thing your team has to keep healthy. When the underlying data changes or your business evolves, the semantic layer has to change in lockstep. That’s where Dex and SLayer change the game. Dex runs SLayer's own validation rules
